items.detail: The **S&P 500** ended Thursday all but flat at **7,704**, and the Nasdaq Composite also closed little changed after trading sharply lower midday.
items.why: A report of talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz offset the day's fresh jump in bond yields.

items.detail: The **10-year Treasury yield** climbed another nine basis points to **5.20%**, a fresh 19-year high and a fourth straight day of selling.
items.why: Traders now put roughly 75% odds on an October Fed hike after this week's hot activity data.

items.detail: **Brent crude spiked about 5% to $108** on Thursday before surrendering most of that gain by the close.
items.why: Houthi missiles hit Saudi Arabia, then Reuters reported Iran may reopen Hormuz if Washington lifts its blockade.

items.detail: **Hong Kong's Hang Seng opened 1% lower** on Friday near **24,523**, extending Thursday's slide to a third session.
items.why: The Trump-Xi summit ended without the expected tariff cuts or AI channel, so traders saw no progress.

items.detail: The **Nifty steadied near 23,100** on Friday after Thursday's 1.64% slide, with IT the heaviest drag at 1.4% lower.
items.why: Foreign investors sold ₹5,027 crore of Indian shares on Thursday as the US 10-year yield hit 5.20%.

items.detail: Investors pulled **$3.3 billion** from the iShares **Russell 2000** ETF last week, its second-largest weekly outflow of 2026.
items.why: US small caps carry more floating-rate debt, so a 5.20% 10-year yield raises their borrowing costs most.

items.detail: **Bitcoin held around $84,300** on Friday as US spot bitcoin funds turned net-positive for 2026, up **$4.6 billion** since August.
items.why: Returning fund demand steadied the price, but 75% odds of an October Fed hike cap any rebound.

items.detail: **Ether slipped to about $2,647** on Thursday, a further 2.5% lower and now a third straight daily loss.
items.why: Bets on a second Fed rate hike by December pulled money out of the riskiest assets first.

items.detail: **Solana held near $115**, roughly flat on the day, as its US ETFs logged a **12th straight week** of inflows.
items.why: Corporate treasuries keep buying SOL, steadying the price even after ETF inflows fell 96% in a week.

items.detail: **Spot gold slipped to about $4,268 an ounce** on Friday, a fourth straight loss, while silver fell below $64.
items.why: A dollar at a near two-month high and firming Fed hike bets keep bullion on the back foot.

crossCuttingTheme: Rising yields remain the only lever that matters: a fourth day of Treasury selling took the 10-year to 5.20%, draining cash from small caps, Asian and Indian equities and gold while capping bitcoin's rebound.
